evidence_items.locator: July 26, 2023 release, Hawley's first quoted paragraph
evidence_items.explanation: Hawley identified protective legislative priorities at a hearing devoted to regulating AI. This supports the claim's description of his 2023 public position, but not a conclusion about the whole party.

evidence_items.explanation: The committee chair openly opposed regulatory restraints and promoted a deregulatory agenda. This supports the leadership-direction component, but comparing Cruz in 2025 with Hawley in 2023 does not measure a party-wide change.

evidence_items.publisher: US House Committee on Energy and Commerce
evidence_items.explanation: Republican leaders endorsed substantive deepfake protections, and the release records a 409–2 House vote. This limits any inference of across-the-board resistance, though it does not disprove increased resistance to broader regulation.

unresolved_gaps: No sufficiently comparable party-wide record was established to measure the size of the change from 2023.
The evidence does not establish how much influence Hawley or similarly positioned Republicans lost by May 16, 2025.
The available examples concern different types of regulation and different Republican officials.
